claims: Artemis II launched successfully on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972.
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II astronauts are circling the Moon in the Orion capsule.
Artemis II lifted off on April 1, 2026, from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Reid Wiseman is the Commander and a NASA astronaut on Artemis II.
Victor Glover is the Pilot and a NASA astronaut on Artemis II.
Christina Koch is a Mission Specialist and a NASA astronaut on Artemis II.
Jeremy Hansen is a Mission Specialist and a CSA astronaut on Artemis II.
The purpose of Artemis II is to test the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
The purpose of Artemis II is to verify the Orion spacecraft's capabilities in deep space with humans aboard.
Artemis II prepares the way for the Artemis III lunar landing.
Orion will perform a multi-day journey following the Artemis II launch.
The Artemis II flight path includes a flyby that takes Orion over 10,000 kilometers beyond the far side of the Moon.
Orion will return to Earth for a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
The duration of Artemis II is approximately 10 days.
The Artemis II crew is testing manual piloting techniques in Earth orbit before proceeding toward the Moon
